title: Wire strippers, 10–18 AWG solid / 12–20 AWG stranded

sources.citation: Electricians' wire strippers marked 10-18 AWG solid on one side of the jaws and 12-20 AWG stranded on the other are a common class made by several makers (typical published markings, paraphrased, not one vendor's). Each physical hole carries a solid size and the stranded size of the next even size, two AWG numbers smaller: a 7-strand concentric conductor of equal area is 3/sqrt(7), about 1.134, times the solid diameter, so stranded 12 AWG is about 2.33 mm across, between solid 11 AWG (2.30 mm) and 10 AWG (2.59 mm), and fits the solid-10 hole (diameters from the AWG formula, NBS Handbook 100 section 2). Modelled as one hole per marking (ten ids, stable save format).

game-design: strippers of this class have cutting edges between the pivot and the holes, modelled as a cut capability up to 10 AWG, the largest hole; the strip capability reaches the same largest marked hole.
